answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by making influence earned, not claimed. Each new identity posts a bond, completes unpredictable tasks, and gathers signatures from reviewers drawn outside its cluster. A dune of verified history must precede every privilege, a quartz ledger records each attestation, and a plume of reputation grows only after repeated agreement. Audits slash false bonds, so multiplying identities raises cost without raising trust.
